name: rowCounts
title: Counts the number of occurrences of a specific value

origin.description: Counts the number of occurrences of a specific value in each row.
origin.usage:
rowCounts(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, value = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE,
  dim. = dim(x), ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The row- and column-wise functions take a matrix or a vector. A vector requires dim. with prod(dim.) == length(x). The result matches matrix(x, nrow = dim.[1], ncol = dim.[2]) without allocating that matrix. Numeric and logical input uses the C routine. A missing value with na.rm = FALSE makes that row's count NA, even when the value was already seen.
origin.value: An integer vector of length N, the number of selected rows. NA is the integer missing value.
origin.example:
x <- matrix(c(0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 2L, 3L, 7L, 8L, 4L, NA_integer_, 11L), nrow = 4)
rowCounts(x, value = 2)

translation.description: Counts the number of occurrences of a specific value in each row.
translation.usage: rowCounts(x, rows=None, cols=None, value=True, na_rm=False, dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix. Logical values are 0, 1, and the integer NA sentinel. Double missing values are nan. Integer missing values are None or -2147483648.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled. A positive index past the end is an error.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. The same index rules as rows apply.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A single value to search for. TRUE on numeric data counts ones for rowCounts and colCounts. For the all and any functions, a logical value on numeric data treats zeros as FALSE and every other non-missing number as TRUE.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm. False keeps a missing value in the tally: a count becomes missing, while all and any stay undecided until a definite false or true is seen.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain array, with no names attached.

translation.details: The scan lives in the Rust crate rowcounts, ported from matrixStats src/rowCounts.c with what 2. Rows are axis 0. A 1-d x with dim is filled column-major. Double NA is nan, and every NaN counts as missing. Integer and logical NA is -2147483648. When na_rm is false, the first missing value in a row sets that count to NA and later cells in the row are skipped.
translation.value: An int32 vector of length N. The integer missing count is -2147483648.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowcounts import rowCounts, colCounts, count

x = np.array([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 7, 8, 4, -2147483648, 11], dtype=np.int32).reshape((4, 3), order="F")
rowCounts(x, value=2)
